phases.name: Establish the safety contract
phases.description: Treat customer safety as the primary invariant, distinguish stated targets from guarantees, and make production experiments explicitly governed.

phases.name: Define and gate experiment requests
phases.description: Version experiment hypotheses, identities, target scopes, approvals, safety policy, concurrency, recommendations, and operator views.

phases.name: Execute through a bounded control path
phases.description: Dispatch only approved experiments through a durable scheduler and isolated runners, while observing targets and returning a fast stop signal.

phases.name: Measure resilience and close the loop
phases.description: Preserve experiment evidence, train suggestions on reviewed outcomes, and produce service scorecards with statistically defensible comparisons.

steps.phase: Establish the safety contract
steps.title: Put the safety invariant before experiment breadth
steps.content: The brief asks to define and safely execute experiments, inject network/CPU/disk/service faults, monitor behavior, halt on safety violations, suggest experiments with ML, track resilience, produce service scorecards, and integrate CI/CD verification. Its safety targets are zero customer-visible impact, a halt within 10 seconds, safeguarded production use, 50+ concurrent experiments, and statistically significant metrics. Zero impact is an objective to defend and measure—not a guarantee an architecture diagram can make.

steps.phase: Establish the safety contract
steps.title: Default to narrow, reversible experiments
steps.content: Use opt-in targets, bounded blast radius, progressive exposure, an independent stop authority, and a safe baseline before considering a production experiment. Define prohibited targets, customer-impact signals, rollback behavior, and authorization ownership before enabling fault injection; the brief does not specify these policies or a workload profile.

steps.phase: Establish the safety contract
steps.title: Keep deployment integration explicit
steps.content: Represent existing CI/CD pipelines as a request source for pre-deployment verification. A pipeline can request an experiment and receive a result, but it cannot bypass target enrollment, policy, approval, or the runtime stop control.

component.label: CI/CD Verification Sources
component.description: Existing deployment pipelines request bounded pre-deployment resilience checks and consume signed, traceable experiment results without bypassing safety policy.

properties.purpose: Existing deployment pipelines request bounded pre-deployment resilience checks and consume signed, traceable experiment results without bypassing safety policy.

component.highlightReason: Integration belongs at the governed request boundary; a deploy hook must not become an unchecked fault-injection path.

steps.phase: Establish the safety contract
steps.title: Provide an operator and approval surface
steps.content: Show experiment scope, hypothesis, risk, approval status, active runs, stop state, and evidence. Require explicit approval for production scope according to policy and make the stop action reachable during a run.

component.label: Experiment Review Console
component.description: Authorized operators review hypotheses, scope, risk, approvals, live safety state, experiment results, and service scorecards; production execution requires explicit governed approval.

properties.purpose: Authorized operators review hypotheses, scope, risk, approvals, live safety state, experiment results, and service scorecards; production execution requires explicit governed approval.

component.highlightReason: The reviewer needs a visible control point for production safeguards and a reachable stop action.

steps.phase: Establish the safety contract
steps.title: Separate experiment control from execution
steps.content: Keep the control plane responsible for definitions and policy decisions, and the runner tier responsible only for an already authorized, bounded action. The execution path must fail closed when authorization, target health, or the safety channel is unavailable.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Authenticate experiment requests
steps.content: Use a single API boundary for console, CI/CD, and approved integrations. Validate schema, identity, idempotency key, target ownership, and request rate before a request can become an experiment record.

component.label: Experiment API Gateway
component.description: Authenticated, rate-controlled entry point validates experiment requests from CI/CD and operators, preserves idempotency, and rejects unauthorized targets.

properties.purpose: Authenticated, rate-controlled entry point validates experiment requests from CI/CD and operators, preserves idempotency, and rejects unauthorized targets.

component.highlightReason: All request sources need the same governed contract, with no direct route to execution workers.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Coordinate experiment lifecycle
steps.content: Normalize requests into a lifecycle with draft, reviewed, approved, scheduled, running, halted, and completed states. Enforce idempotent transitions and retain actor, target, policy version, and correlation ID for every decision.

component.label: Experiment Control Plane
component.description: Coordinates experiment lifecycle, policy evaluation, approvals, target enrollment, idempotent state transitions, and result delivery for console and CI/CD clients.

properties.purpose: Coordinates experiment lifecycle, policy evaluation, approvals, target enrollment, idempotent state transitions, and result delivery for console and CI/CD clients.

component.highlightReason: One lifecycle owner prevents alternate request paths from skipping approval or leaving ambiguous active runs.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Keep an auditable experiment registry
steps.content: Persist the hypothesis, experiment type, target scope, planned severity, approval evidence, safety policy version, run history, and final outcome. The brief does not state retention or tenant count, so size and retention remain to be agreed.

component.label: Experiment and Target Registry
component.description: Auditable definitions and run records capture hypotheses, fault category, target enrollment, scope, approvals, policy versions, lifecycle, and verified outcomes.

properties.purpose: Auditable definitions and run records capture hypotheses, fault category, target enrollment, scope, approvals, policy versions, lifecycle, and verified outcomes.

component.highlightReason: The registry is the source of truth for what was authorized, where it ran, and what evidence supports a resilience claim.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Place an independent safety gate
steps.content: Evaluate target allowlists, blast-radius limits, current service health, approval evidence, customer-impact signals, and stop conditions independently from experiment selection. Safety checks must be re-evaluated immediately before dispatch and continuously during execution.

component.label: Safety Policy and Kill Switch
component.description: Independent policy gate enforces enrolled targets, scope limits, production approvals, health preconditions, customer-impact guards, expiry, and an operator kill switch.

properties.purpose: Independent policy gate enforces enrolled targets, scope limits, production approvals, health preconditions, customer-impact guards, expiry, and an operator kill switch.

component.highlightReason: A separate safety authority makes abort and production safeguards independent of the recommendation model and scheduler.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Schedule only eligible experiments
steps.content: Admit experiments only after the safety gate allows them. Enforce per-service concurrency, staged severity, resource budgets, and cancellation deadlines; queue or reject excess work rather than weakening isolation to hit a concurrency count.

component.label: Bounded Experiment Scheduler
component.description: Schedules approved experiments with per-target concurrency limits, staged exposure, resource budgets, expiry, cancellation, and backpressure for the 50+ concurrency target.

properties.purpose: Schedules approved experiments with per-target concurrency limits, staged exposure, resource budgets, expiry, cancellation, and backpressure for the 50+ concurrency target.

component.highlightReason: The 50+ concurrent target is achieved through measured admission and isolation, not by allowing conflicting tests on the same target.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Dispatch through a replayable command channel
steps.content: Publish scoped run and cancellation events with experiment ID, target identity, expiry, and policy revision. Ensure a repeated delivery cannot extend a fault or restart a stopped run.

component.label: Experiment Command and Event Bus
component.description: Durable commands and lifecycle events coordinate approved execution, cancellation, status, and evidence while allowing the scheduler and consumers to recover independently.

properties.purpose: Durable commands and lifecycle events coordinate approved execution, cancellation, status, and evidence while allowing the scheduler and consumers to recover independently.

component.highlightReason: The channel supports independent execution workers and reliable stop/status propagation under concurrent runs.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Use constrained execution runners
steps.content: Runners accept only typed, expiring commands for enrolled targets and approved fault classes. Keep implementation-specific privileges outside the user-facing guide; isolate runner permissions and make execution observable and cancellable.

component.label: Isolated Experiment Runners
component.description: Constrained workers execute approved network, CPU, disk, or service-failure experiment classes against explicitly enrolled targets, with expiry, cancellation, and scoped permissions.

properties.purpose: Constrained workers execute approved network, CPU, disk, or service-failure experiment classes against explicitly enrolled targets, with expiry, cancellation, and scoped permissions.

component.highlightReason: Fault execution is isolated behind a typed command and least-privilege runner boundary.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Limit experiments to enrolled services
steps.content: Represent the participating service estate and its health/safety integrations. Production targets require explicit enrollment, ownership, supported stop signals, and a recovery path; absence of these facts blocks execution.

component.label: Enrolled Service Targets
component.description: Existing services opt in with owner, permitted experiment scope, health signals, and recovery integration; unregistered or unsupported production targets are not eligible.

properties.purpose: Existing services opt in with owner, permitted experiment scope, health signals, and recovery integration; unregistered or unsupported production targets are not eligible.

component.highlightReason: An explicit enrollment boundary reduces blast radius and makes production safeguards enforceable.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Observe service health and experiment signals
steps.content: Collect baseline and during-run health signals, experiment events, customer-impact indicators, and recovery status. The exact signals and thresholds must be selected per service; no universal threshold is assumed by this draft.

component.label: Experiment Safety Monitoring
component.description: Correlates service health, customer-impact guardrails, experiment lifecycle, and recovery signals in real time for policy evaluation and resilience analysis.

properties.purpose: Correlates service health, customer-impact guardrails, experiment lifecycle, and recovery signals in real time for policy evaluation and resilience analysis.

component.highlightReason: Monitoring must watch the target and the experiment itself; the safety gate depends on both.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Retain experiment measurements and outcomes
steps.content: Store baseline, treatment, guardrail, stop, and recovery observations with run and service identifiers. Preserve control/treatment assignment and measurement-window metadata so statistical analysis can distinguish evidence from anecdote.

component.label: Resilience Measurement Store
component.description: Versioned run measurements preserve baseline and treatment observations, customer-impact signals, stop/recovery events, service identity, and analysis provenance.

properties.purpose: Versioned run measurements preserve baseline and treatment observations, customer-impact signals, stop/recovery events, service identity, and analysis provenance.

component.highlightReason: Statistical significance and later trend comparisons require retained, attributable measurements and methodology.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Train suggestions from reviewed evidence
steps.content: Train candidate recommendations on reviewed experiment outcomes and known coverage gaps. Treat suggestions as hypotheses for human or policy review, not automatic authority to execute; evaluate for bias toward risky targets and stale results.

component.label: Experiment Recommendation Training
component.description: Offline pipeline builds candidate-experiment recommendations from reviewed hypotheses, observed resilience gaps, and time-correct outcomes with safety-focused evaluation.

properties.purpose: Offline pipeline builds candidate-experiment recommendations from reviewed hypotheses, observed resilience gaps, and time-correct outcomes with safety-focused evaluation.

component.highlightReason: Recommendations should be evidence-backed and independently checked by the safety policy before scheduling.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Serve advisory experiment candidates
steps.content: Return a suggested hypothesis, rationale, relevant service evidence, model version, and uncertainty. Do not allow the recommender to create a runnable command or bypass approval.

component.label: Experiment Candidate Recommender
component.description: Versioned advisory model ranks candidate resilience hypotheses from reviewed evidence and returns rationale, uncertainty, and provenance without dispatch authority.

properties.purpose: Versioned advisory model ranks candidate resilience hypotheses from reviewed evidence and returns rationale, uncertainty, and provenance without dispatch authority.

component.highlightReason: Model output remains advisory; deterministic safety policy and authorization own execution decisions.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Summarize results by service
steps.content: Produce service-level scorecards from reviewed evidence, showing coverage, resilience hypothesis, baseline, measured response, confidence/uncertainty, and known limitations. Avoid a single opaque score that hides sample size or customer-impact events.

component.label: Resilience Analytics
component.description: Analyzes experiment coverage, baseline and treatment measurements, recovery, safety events, and uncertainty to produce comparable service-level resilience evidence.

properties.purpose: Analyzes experiment coverage, baseline and treatment measurements, recovery, safety events, and uncertainty to produce comparable service-level resilience evidence.

component.highlightReason: Statistical significance requires an explicit comparison and visible uncertainty, not just an aggregate score.

steps.phase: Define and gate experiment requests
steps.title: Present scorecards and active safety state
steps.content: Expose authorized experiment lifecycle, service health, stop state, recommendations, and scorecards in one operator surface. Keep emergency actions prominent and require confirmation for irreversible administrative changes.

component.label: Resilience Scorecards
component.description: Authorized views display experiment status, safety/stop state, reviewed recommendations, and evidence-rich resilience scorecards for each service.

properties.purpose: Authorized views display experiment status, safety/stop state, reviewed recommendations, and evidence-rich resilience scorecards for each service.

component.highlightReason: The scorecard should expose its supporting evidence and safety status rather than overstate readiness.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Accept CI/CD requests at the governed edge
steps.content: Pipeline requests use the same authenticated boundary as operator requests and identify the deployment, target scope, and intended verification window.

connection.label: Pre-deployment verification request
connection.description: Idempotent request carries deployment identity, enrolled target, hypothesis, and correlation metadata.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Submit operator-reviewed requests
steps.content: The console submits a proposed experiment or approval decision through the same API, retaining actor and approval evidence.

connection.label: Reviewed experiment request
connection.description: Authenticated operator action includes target scope, approval context, and idempotency key.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Route requests to the lifecycle owner
steps.content: The gateway forwards only validated, authorized requests to the control plane, which owns lifecycle and policy evaluation.

connection.label: Validated experiment request
connection.description: Tenant, actor, target enrollment, request ID, and policy-relevant context are preserved.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Persist every decision and lifecycle transition
steps.content: Record request, approval, policy version, run status, and outcome before acknowledging state changes. Retries must not create a second active experiment for the same idempotency key.

connection.label: Audited lifecycle and policy record
connection.description: Versioned experiment definition, target, approval evidence, state transition, and result references.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Check safety before scheduling
steps.content: The control plane asks the independent safety service to validate current target health, scope, approvals, active-run limits, and the requested experiment class. A denial remains a first-class outcome.

connection.label: Preflight safety authorization
connection.description: Short-lived decision binds the approved scope, target, policy version, and expiry.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Release only approved work to the scheduler
steps.content: Only a current, scoped safety authorization is sent for scheduling. The scheduler rechecks expiry and target limits immediately before dispatch.

connection.label: Approved bounded run
connection.description: Authorization token binds experiment ID, target scope, fault class, maximum exposure, and expiry.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Publish run and cancellation commands
steps.content: The scheduler emits an expiring run command and can publish cancellation without waiting for a reporting consumer. Use consumer acknowledgements and expiry to handle stalled runners safely.

connection.label: Scoped run and cancel events
connection.description: Commands include run ID, enrolled target, approved scope, policy revision, and expiry.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Dispatch bounded commands to isolated runners
steps.content: Workers consume only commands valid for their enrolled target and supported experiment class. Concurrency limits apply both globally and per target to avoid competing experiments.

connection.label: Expiring experiment commands
connection.description: Idempotent work delivery with bounded concurrency and acknowledgement of start, completion, or cancellation.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Apply an approved experiment to its target
steps.content: A runner applies only the approved, bounded test to the enrolled service and reports the run ID. If the target identity or authorization differs, reject the command.

connection.label: Scoped experiment execution
connection.description: Restricted execution interface enforces target identity, authorized fault class, expiry, and cancellation.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Observe target and customer-impact signals
steps.content: The monitor receives baseline, active-run, and recovery signals from enrolled targets; define alert thresholds with service owners rather than assuming one global SLO.

connection.label: Health and impact telemetry
connection.description: Time-stamped service health, customer-impact guardrails, recovery state, and experiment correlation ID.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Send stop signals to the independent gate
steps.content: A safety violation reaches the independent kill switch directly. Measure detection-to-stop end-to-end, including signal collection, policy decision, cancellation propagation, and runner acknowledgement, against the 10-second target.

connection.label: Safety breach signal
connection.description: Correlated breach event carries observed condition, target, active run, event time, and severity.

steps.phase: Execute through a bounded control path
steps.title: Measure the stop path as one safety channel
steps.content: The safety-to-scheduler control edge carries both a short-lived authorization and its revocation/cancel signal. Keep the independent safety decision on this path and measure breach detection through runner acknowledgement; a separate duplicate edge would obscure rather than strengthen the stop guarantee.

steps.phase: Measure resilience and close the loop
steps.title: Store execution events for audit
steps.content: Persist command, start, progress, cancel, and completion events so the experiment record can be reconciled even after a consumer restart.

connection.label: Run lifecycle evidence
connection.description: Replayable experiment events keyed by run, target, and policy revision.

steps.phase: Measure resilience and close the loop
steps.title: Retain monitored measurements
steps.content: Write baseline, treatment, guardrail, safety, and recovery measurements with timestamps and run identity. Keep raw evidence and derived summaries distinguishable.

connection.label: Time-series experiment evidence
connection.description: Correlated health and customer-impact observations with baseline/treatment windows and monitor provenance.

steps.phase: Measure resilience and close the loop
steps.title: Train on reviewed experiment outcomes
steps.content: Only reviewed hypotheses, service gaps, and verified outcomes enter the training corpus; preserve temporal splits and avoid leakage from later incidents into a recommendation.

connection.label: Reviewed resilience evidence
connection.description: Versioned experiment outcomes and service context with review status and time-correct labels.

steps.phase: Measure resilience and close the loop
steps.title: Promote evaluated advisory models
steps.content: Model promotion requires safety-focused offline evaluation and a versioned evidence record. Recommendations remain advisory after promotion.

connection.label: Reviewed recommendation model
connection.description: Versioned candidate model with evaluation, uncertainty, and provenance metadata.

steps.phase: Measure resilience and close the loop
steps.title: Return candidates for policy review
steps.content: Suggestions go to the control plane as proposals only. They still require target enrollment, policy checks, and the normal approval workflow.

connection.label: Advisory experiment candidates
connection.description: Ranked hypotheses with rationale, uncertainty, model version, and supporting reviewed evidence.

steps.phase: Measure resilience and close the loop
steps.title: Calculate evidence-based resilience summaries
steps.content: Analytics compares defined baselines and outcomes with sample size and uncertainty. A statistically significant result requires a declared hypothesis, comparison method, stopping rule, and metric; these are not specified by the brief.

connection.label: Baseline and treatment evidence
connection.description: Reviewed measurements, safety events, sample/window metadata, and experiment methodology.

steps.phase: Measure resilience and close the loop
steps.title: Include current safety telemetry in analysis
steps.content: Analytics includes guardrail breaches, halts, and recovery time, not only successful experiment outcomes; otherwise a scorecard could reward unsafe experiments.

connection.label: Safety and recovery outcomes
connection.description: Observed impact, breach, halt, and recovery evidence joined by experiment and service identity.

steps.phase: Measure resilience and close the loop
steps.title: Publish per-service scorecards
steps.content: The scorecard links each claim to the experiment, cohort, baseline, measurement window, uncertainty, and safety events, and labels untested areas as unknown rather than resilient.

connection.label: Evidence-backed service scorecards
connection.description: Service-level summaries with methodology, experiment coverage, confidence/uncertainty, and limitations.

steps.phase: Measure resilience and close the loop
steps.title: Show lifecycle and stop status to operators
steps.content: The control plane publishes current run, approval, and cancellation state to the console so operators can act on current rather than stale status.

connection.label: Authorized run and safety status
connection.description: Current lifecycle, active target scope, approval state, and stop/cancel result.

steps.phase: Measure resilience and close the loop
steps.title: Validate safety and concurrency empirically
steps.content: Test failure of the monitor, policy service, broker, runner, and cancellation acknowledgement; each should fail closed or stop safely. Measure breach-detection-to-runner-stop under the 10-second target, demonstrate at least 50 concurrent experiments without exceeding per-target limits, and use an agreed statistical method. Do not claim zero customer impact from a successful test alone.
